answer: Persistent neighbor lag. Agents record which peers stay reachable across epochs. New identities must cross a lagoon of unproven latency: their routes start on a probationary ledge with limited forwarding. To gain normal standing, an attacker must keep each fake agent continuously online and mutually reachable for many epochs, building a costly bridge of sustained connectivity. Enforcement: only long-lived reciprocal edges count, so each identity pays real bandwidth and uptime.
